subject: RE: Redwood vs Hyperscaler benchmarks — next steps & p95/p99 follow-up
messages:
From: Amit Shah <amit.shah@globex.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@gmail>
Cc: Katrina Lopez <katrina.lopez@globex.com>
Date: 2026-03-15T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood benchmark run — initial data attached

Hi Marissa / team,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — super helpful. I ran a quick pass of our current inference traffic against Hyperscaler X (their hosted API) and attached the initial p95/p99 exports (redwood-vs-hyperscaler-p95-p99.csv). The high-level observations:

- Hyperscaler shows more stable median latency, but p99 spikes on long prompts (1k+ tokens).
- Tokens/sec on Hyperscaler varies a lot by concurrency; our live workload runs many short and mid-length prompts.

We want to get a direct A/B comparison against Redwood with the same workload. Can you confirm whether Redwood can run the same workload in our staging (we prefer testing from our VPC) or if you recommend running your hosted sandbox?

Also: we care most about p95/p99 and tokens/sec under sustained load (5–10k RPS burst) — our target p99 for interactive features is <250ms.

Attached the CSV and a brief perf export. Let me know what you need (keys, sample prompts, test harness). Also looping in Katrina (platform) to coordinate.

Thanks,
Amit Shah
Head of ML Platform
Globex Corp
[attachment: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-p95-p99.csv]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@gmail>

Subject: RE: Redwood benchmark run — initial data attached

Hi Amit — great context and thanks for sharing the CSV. Recap from our side + proposed next steps: 

Recap (post-call):
- Goal: apples-to-apples A/B of Redwood Hosted/Dedicated vs Hyperscaler X for your production workload focusing on p95/p99 and sustained tokens/sec.
- Constraints: you prefer staging runs from your VPC; target p99 <250ms for interactive paths.

Proposed next steps (we can start once we have your sample prompt set and test harness):
1) Test plan: run 3-day A/B with identical request traces (shuffle-seeded), measure p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and tail latencies by prompt length buckets (0-128, 128-512, 512-2048).
2) Env: we recommend running Redwood in your staging VPC (Private deployment) for parity. If that's not feasible, our hosted sandbox will be configured to mirror your region/hardware.
3) Configs we will use: the same open model you used for Hyperscaler (please confirm model name + quantization); Redwood will test both FP16 and quantized variants and report differences.
4) Deliverables: consolidated CSV, dashboard link, per-route regression notes, and a wrap-up call to decide next steps.

What we need from you to start:
- sample_prompts.json or a test harness we can point at (S3 or staging host)
- which model + any custom tokenizer or pre/post-processing
- access method (we can run agents in your VPC or provide a lightweight test container)

Connor will share the exact test script and warm-up methodology. Rishi will coordinate timeline and resourcing.

Proposed slots for a short 30-min alignment call: Tue 3/17 10:00–10:30am PT or Wed 3/18 2:00–2:30pm PT. Which works for you?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
redwood.com

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@gmail>
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@globex.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@gmail>
Cc: Katrina Lopez <katrina.lopez@globex.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@gmail>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@gmail>
Date: 2026-03-17T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Redwood benchmark run — initial data attached (test plan + scripts)

Hi all — Connor from Redwood infra. Quick technical details for parity testing and attached instructions (a-b-test-instructions.pdf). Key points: 

Test methodology (summary):
- Workload: replay identical request traces with original timing preserved (we use a replay tool that respects inter-arrival times).
- Warm-up: 30 minutes at 50% peak to populate KV caches and stabilize JIT/kernels.
- Measurement windows: 1) steady state (after warm-up) 2) burst windows (simulate 5–10k RPS for 1 minute).
- Metrics collected: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cpu/gpu util, queue depth, and per-token micro-latency.
- Prompt buckets: 0–128, 128–512, 512–2048 tokens to capture tail behavior.

Runtime notes (why results may differ):
- Continuous batching: Redwood's runtime batches in-flight requests; tokens/sec improves at moderate concurrency but can increase p95 if batch timeout not tuned. We'll surface both tuned and conservative configs.
- KV cache effects: if your workload has repeated prefixes, KV cache will dramatically help p99 for long sequences — we will run both cold and warm cache scenarios.
- Model variants: please confirm exact model name (we saw you listed "gptx-3.1-large-fp16" in notes). We'll test FP16 and int8 quantized variants.

Execution options:
1) Run test agents in your staging VPC (recommended) — we will provide a small container and IAM role.
2) Run from Redwood hosted sandbox in us-west with identical hardware profile (we'll supply reserve capacity).

Action items for Globex: share sample_prompts.json, confirm model name and whether you want warm-cache only or both, and confirm whether you can provide ephemeral staging creds.

Attachments: a-b-test-instructions.pdf (contains scripts, curl examples, and expected CSV format).

Thanks — Connor
Principal Software Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: a-b-test-instructions.pdf]

From: Amit Shah <amit.shah@globex.com>

Thanks, Marissa and Connor — this is exactly the level of detail we need. Quick answers / confirmations: 

- We'll run the replay from our staging VPC and can provide ephemeral creds for a 48-hour window.
- Model: we used gptx-3.1-large-fp16 on Hyperscaler X; please include int8 quant variant if you support it.
- We want both cold-cache and warm-cache windows; p99 is the priority metric — our SLO target is <250ms for interactive features.

We can share sample_prompts.json via a secure S3 link by EOD 3/20. Please confirm you can start the run on 3/21 and provide estimated ETA for consolidated results (how long after the 3-day A/B run can we expect the dashboard + CSV?).

Also can you confirm which Redwood-hosted model variant maps to our gptx-3.1-large-fp16 naming so we know we're comparing the same weights. HubSpot ticket: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/ticket/78901

Let's schedule the wrap-up call for Tue 3/24 11:00am PT — works on our side if that works for you.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Amit
Head of ML Platform, Globex
